1. The Beginning

Genesis 1:1

1. The Beginning

Genesis 1:1

The story of Jesus fits within the larger story of the Judeo Christian tradition. The purpose of everything since creation has been to point to the life of Jesus. All of creation speaks of the majesty of God. As God created man and woman he intended them to live in peace with him forever. But because of their disobedience mankind was separated from God. But God still loved mankind so throughout the Scriptures God reveals his plan to save the world.

3:43
2. Birth Of Jesus

Luke 1:1

2. Birth Of Jesus

Luke 1:1

Luke makes his introduction as the careful author of this Gospel. The angel Gabriel appears to Mary, a virgin in Nazareth. He announces to her that she has found favor with God and will give birth to Jesus, the Son of God. Through Jesus' birth, prophecies are fulfilled by the arrangement of events. God leaves no detail unnoticed. The same can be said of our own lives.

2:15
3. Childhood Of Jesus

Luke 2:21

3. Childhood Of Jesus

Luke 2:21

One week after the baby is born, He is circumcised and officially named Jesus. While Jesus is a small boy they go to the temple where they meet a man named Simeon. The Holy Spirit had assured Simeon he would not die before seeing the Lord's Messiah. Simeon sees Jesus and declares Him the promised Messiah.

3:47
4. Baptism Of Jesus By John

Luke 3:1

4. Baptism Of Jesus By John

Luke 3:1

John the Baptist calls out in the desert. He preaches by the river Jordan, "Turn away from your sins and be baptized, and God will forgive your sins." He is the one Isaiah predicted would make way for the Lord. The crowds gather. Immediately, he warns them not to only say they have repented. Instead, they're to follow repentance with actions that exhibit a changed heart. Jesus is baptized and receives the Holy Spirit. He kneels at the feet of someone lesser than Himself to be baptized. He demonstrates how we are to be humble.

2:22
5. The Devil Tempts Jesus

Luke 4:1

5. The Devil Tempts Jesus

Luke 4:1

After Jesus has been baptized, He's led by the Spirit into the desert. He spends 40 days there, constantly tempted by the devil. All that time, he eats nothing. The devil tries to tempt Jesus, but Jesus answers using Scripture, resisting him.

3:07
6. Jesus Proclaims Fulfillment Of The Scriptures

Luke 4:14

6. Jesus Proclaims Fulfillment Of The Scriptures

Luke 4:14

When Jesus returns to Nazareth, He goes to the synagogue. He's asked to read the Scriptures and is handed the Book of Isaiah. From it, He reads Isaiah 61:1-2. The prophecy speaks of bringing good news to the poor, proclaiming liberty to the captives, recovery of sight to the blind, freeing the oppressed, and announcing that it's time the Lord will save His people. When He finishes reading, Jesus announces to the people that the prophecy has come true as it was just read.

1:02
7. Parable Of The Pharisee And Tax Collector

Luke 18:9

7. Parable Of The Pharisee And Tax Collector

Luke 18:9

Jesus teaches from a boat off the shore of Lake Gennesaret. He speaks in parables, giving the example of a Pharisee and tax collector going to the temple to pray. The two men approach prayer very differently. The Pharisee in the story stands by himself and lists his respectable attributes. He thanks God that he is not greedy, dishonest, or an adulterer like everyone else. He specifically points out the tax collector and thanks God for not being like him. The Pharisee boldly tells God what he does: He fasts two days a week and gives a tenth of his income. The tax collector stands at a distance from the altar. Head bowed, he beats on his chest. The only thing he prays is, "God, have pity on me, a sinner!"

2:01
8. Miraculous Catch Of Fish

Luke 5:1

8. Miraculous Catch Of Fish

Luke 5:1

Jesus tells the fisherman who owns it to push out farther and let down their nets. The fisherman grumbles that he and the others have already been out all night long. They didn't catch anything. The fisherman agrees to go out and calls to his partners. Jesus sits in the boat with the fisherman. He waits expectantly. Then gathers the nets, slowly bringing something to the surface. He laughs with joy when he sees the nets are full of flopping fish. When they're done, the fisherman sits in a boat full of fish. He looks up to Jesus. The fisherman frowns and says, "Go away from me, Lord. I am a sinful man." Jesus tells him not to be afraid, that from then on, he would be a fisher of men.

2:14
9. Jairuss Daughter Brought Back To Life

Luke 8:41

9. Jairuss Daughter Brought Back To Life

Luke 8:41

Crowds press in on Jesus as He leaves the synagogue. One voice rises above the others. A man, Jairus, begs Jesus to save his sick, 12-year-old daughter. Another man runs up to Jairus. He tells him not to bother the teacher, that his daughter has died. Jesus turns and tells him not to be afraid. And that if Jairus would believe, his daughter would be well. Jesus and the disciples visit the family. The neighbors wail for the loss of the daughter. She lies lifeless on a cot. Jesus looks at her for a moment. Then He looks to the child’s mother and comforts her. He says the child isn't dead, but that she’s actually just asleep. Jesus sits and looks at the girl for a moment, then tells her to rise.

3:10
10. Disciples Chosen

Luke 5:27

10. Disciples Chosen

Luke 5:27

Jesus spots a tax collector named Matthew Levi at the gate. He collects toll money for customs as people pass through. As Jesus looks at him, Matthew senses it and looks up. Jesus says, "Follow me." Matthew watches Him go for a moment. Silently, he stands and leaves everything to follow Jesus. Later Jesus goes up a hill to pray. He prays the entire night to God. When He comes down from the hill the next morning, He gathers His followers. From them, he chooses 12 apostles. Simon (who Jesus named Peter) and Simon's brother Andrew had been the fishermen who experienced the miracle of a large catch of fish. Then Jesus chooses James and John, Philip and Bartholomew. And He chooses Matthew, the tax collector he had called at the gate. And finally Jesus chooses Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who would betray Jesus.

1:02
11. Beatitudes

Luke 6:20

11. Beatitudes

Luke 6:20

Jesus looks out over the crowds gathered to hear him speak. But instead of speaking to the masses, Jesus turns back to his disciples. He encourages them for the journey ahead. He assures them that they are blessed when people hate them, reject them, insult them, and say that they are evil because they follow Jesus. He encourages them to be happy and dance for joy when that happens. Because there will be great reward in heaven for them. And He reminds them that their ancestors acted the same way toward prophets.

3:39
12. Sermon On The Mount

Luke 6:24

12. Sermon On The Mount

Luke 6:24

Jesus turns to the crowds and walks through them, teaching. He advises everyone how to walk through life in love. And talks of how, out of pride, we often judge others. He implores those who are listening to love their enemies, to actively pray for them. He speaks of offering more than what is asked of you. Do for others what you would have them do for you.

0:19
13. Blessed Are Those Who Hear And Obey

Luke 11:27

13. Blessed Are Those Who Hear And Obey

Luke 11:27

Jesus reminds us that those who hear and obey are blessed.

2:56
14. Sinful Woman Forgiven

Luke 7:36

14. Sinful Woman Forgiven

Luke 7:36

A Pharisee invites Jesus to have dinner at His house. They're eating when a woman approaches Jesus. Everyone in the house stares, including the Pharisee. Jesus tells the Pharisee a story. He says that there were two men who owed money to someone. One owed 500 silver coins. The other owed 50. Neither men could pay their debt. So the lender canceled both debts. Jesus asks which man loved the lender more for what he'd done.

0:43
15. Women Disciples

Luke 8:1

15. Women Disciples

Luke 8:1

Jesus continues through the countryside. He's adamant in preaching the good news about the kingdom of God. The twelve disciples follow him. And some women follow as well. They serve the disciples, using their own resources to aid the ministry of Jesus.

1:56
16. John The Baptist In Prison

Luke 7:1

16. John The Baptist In Prison

Luke 7:1

Herod has thrown John the Baptist into prison. Messengers come to him in the prison. They relay to him all that Jesus has been doing. Specifically, they tell him about a funeral procession where Jesus sees the widow who has lost her son. His heart fills with compassion. He tells the young man to get up! The son rises from the dead and goes back with his mother. After hearing this, John asks them to go ask Jesus if He's the Messiah, or if they should expect someone else. The messengers arrive where Jesus is sleeping and ask Him what John wants to know.

2:18
17. Parable Of The Sower And The Seed

Luke 8:4

17. Parable Of The Sower And The Seed

Luke 8:4

The crowds press in on Jesus as He walks and teaches. He tells a parable of someone sowing seeds of grain in a field. The seed falls in a number of places, each representing something to the crowd. A disciple asks Jesus why He speaks in parables. Jesus explains the parable to the disciples. The seed that's scattered is the Word of God.

0:55
18. Parable Of The Lamp

Luke 11:33

18. Parable Of The Lamp

Luke 11:33

Jesus uses a torch to explain how his followers should live. No one covers the light or puts it under a bed. Instead, they put it in a place where people will see the light when they come in. He goes on to say that whatever is kept a secret will be brought into the open. And anything that's covered up will be found and brought into the light.

1:58
19. Jesus Calms The Storm

Luke 8:22

19. Jesus Calms The Storm

Luke 8:22

Jesus gets into a boat and tells His disciples they should all go to the other side of the lake. Along the way, Jesus falls asleep. A storm starts to rage. Waves stretch high over the bow. And the boat starts to take on water. The whole time, Jesus stays asleep. The disciples hold on tight. They try to keep the boat afloat. Finally, Peter cries out to the still sleeping Jesus. He tells Jesus that the boat is taking on water and that they'll all be drowned. Jesus stands and puts a hand out toward the storm. The storm clears. And the seas immediately calm.

2:16
20. Healing Of The Demoniac

Luke 8:26

20. Healing Of The Demoniac

Luke 8:26

Jesus and His disciples continue to sail and arrive at Gerasa. A wild man on the shore growls at their approach. Jesus hurries toward him, ahead of His disciples. The man threatens Jesus with the rock. But Jesus just continues to stare at him. The man calls Jesus by name and declares Him to be the Son of God. Jesus asks him his name. At first the man won't say. But Jesus holds out a hand to him. He says his name is Legion. He begs not to be sent back to the abyss. Instead, he wants to go into a nearby herd of pigs. Jesus puts a hand out to the pigs.

2:29
21. Jesus Feeds 5000

Luke 9:1

21. Jesus Feeds 5000

Luke 9:1

Jesus and the disciples continue to walk the countryside. And a great crowd follows them. Peter comes and asks Jesus to send the people away. He wants them to find food and a place to stay with local farmers and villagers. Jesus looks back out over the crowd of people. They want to hear from Jesus and have sacrificed to be there. Jesus considers this and tells the disciples to feed the people. Mary Magdalene points out that they only have a few loaves of bread and two fish. Jesus takes the baskets and proclaims to the heavens and the people, "Blessed is the Lord God, King of the Universe who brings forth bread from the earth."

1:23
22. Peter Declares Jesus To Be The Christ

Luke 9:18

22. Peter Declares Jesus To Be The Christ

Luke 9:18

Jesus asks who the crowds say He is. Peter speaks up immediately. He claims that some in the crowds say Jesus is John the Baptist. Others say He's Elijah. Others say that one of the prophets from centuries ago has come back to life. Jesus solemnly asks who Peter would say He is. Without hesitation, Peter says Jesus is God's Messiah. Jesus stares back at him.

1:45
23. The Transfiguration

Luke 9:28

23. The Transfiguration

Luke 9:28

Jesus takes John, James and Peter up a hill to pray. Jesus walks apart from them, covering His head to pray. But when He does, His appearance changes. His face changes. His clothes become pure white. He starts talking to two men who seem to be with Him. Moses and Elijah speak to Him. One says Jesus will fulfill God's purpose. The other says He will die in Jerusalem. Peter slowly wakes up. He's the first to see Moses and Elijah talking with Jesus. He wakes James and John. They see it too. Moses and Elijah turn and leave, fading away. The disciples fall to their knees and worship Jesus.

2:15
24. Jesus Heals Boy From Evil Spirit

Luke 9:37

24. Jesus Heals Boy From Evil Spirit

Luke 9:37

The crowds continue to gather. They wait on Jesus. Finally, Jesus comes down the hill with Peter, James and John. One man approaches Jesus and begs that Jesus would heal his son. The boy writhes on the ground. The man goes on to say that the boy is his only son. He asked the disciples to cast out the demon. But they couldn't. Jesus gently tells the man to bring his son closer. Two men carry the boy to Jesus. But he falls again into another fit. Jesus comes to stand over him. The boy looks up. And slowly, he gets up. Now, where there were cuts and bruises on his face, there are none.

0:57
25. The Lords Prayer

Luke 11:1

25. The Lords Prayer

Luke 11:1

The followers of Jesus clean up and take a break at a stream. Jesus stands nearby, praying. Andrew asks Jesus to teach them to pray.

2:23
26. Teaching About Prayer And Faith

Luke 11:5

26. Teaching About Prayer And Faith

Luke 11:5

Jesus has just taught them how to pray. He says, "ask and you will receive." He implores them to seek and assures that they will find. He reminds His followers that none of them would give their children bad things when they ask for good things. He says that no matter how bad mankind is, we still know to give good gifts to our children. And that the Heavenly Father will all the more give the Holy Spirit to those who ask.

0:55
27. Woe To Those Who Cause Others To Sin

Luke 17:5

27. Woe To Those Who Cause Others To Sin

Luke 17:5

As Jesus and the disciples continue to walk the countryside he tells them that there will be temptation. There will be situations which cause people to sin. But the disciples should never be the cause. He looks into the crowd and says it would be better for that person to have a large stone hung around his neck and be tossed into the sea. That would be better than causing someone else to stumble in or lose their faith.

0:28
28. The Kingdom Of God As A Mustard Seed

Luke 17:6

28. The Kingdom Of God As A Mustard Seed

Luke 17:6

Jesus tells the people that the kingdom of God is like a grain of mustard seed. Farmers plant seeds in their field. From it, a tree grows. And when the tree is big enough, birds sit in its branches.

0:29
29. Jesus Spends Time With Sinners

Luke 5:31

29. Jesus Spends Time With Sinners

Luke 5:31

As Jesus sits with a group of people in a village a man walks up and angrily asks why Jesus sits with those who aren't respectable people. Jesus responds that people who are well don't need a doctor. He hasn't come to ask "respectable" people to ask forgiveness for what they do. But He would ask the outcasts to seek and find forgiveness.

1:57
30. Healing On The Sabbath

Luke 13:10

30. Healing On The Sabbath

Luke 13:10

A boy asks Jesus to tell them more about the kingdom. Jesus teaches in the synagogue that believers shouldn't fear. That God is pleased to give them the kingdom. They can feel free to give because their treasure is somewhere else. He urges them to sell their possessions and give to people. He insists that they can make a treasure in heaven that will never wear out. He says that the treasure follows the heart and where it is.

1:38
31. Parable Of The Good Samaritan

Luke 10:25

31. Parable Of The Good Samaritan

Luke 10:25

A man asks Jesus what they should do. Jesus asks what the Scriptures say. The man replies with, "Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind, and love your neighbor as yourself." Jesus tells him that if they do this, they will have life. But then someone asks, "Who is my neighbor?"

1:44
32. Healing Of Bartimaeus

Luke 18:35

32. Healing Of Bartimaeus

Luke 18:35

Jesus and His disciples wade through a stream into a gathering of people. A man asks what's going on. He follows after Jesus, calling out to Him. John comes back for the man and helps him back to Jesus. The blind man calls Jesus the Son of David and begs for mercy. Jesus asks what the man wants Him to do. And the man answers that he would like to see again.

2:21
33. Jesus And Zaccheus

Luke 19:1

33. Jesus And Zaccheus

Luke 19:1

Jesus enters the town surrounded by crowds pushing in on Him. Zacchaeus, a short man, tries to see Jesus. But he can't see above the crowds or get through them. He climbs a tree. Jesus calls out to him. He tells Zacchaeus to come down from the tree because He wants to have dinner with him. People are appalled. Zacchaeus is the town tax collector. But Zacchaeus is more than happy. He comes down from the tree and leads the way.

0:42
34. Jesus Predicts His Death And Resurrection

Luke 18:31

34. Jesus Predicts His Death And Resurrection

Luke 18:31

Jesus continues to sit at dinner with His disciples. He asks them to listen carefully. He tells them plainly that they're all going to Jerusalem with Him. And that everything the prophets wrote about the Son of Man will come true.

1:10
35. Jesuss Triumphal Entry

Luke 19:28

35. Jesuss Triumphal Entry

Luke 19:28

ark in Kikamba, issued in 1850 under the title Evangelio ta yunaolete Malkosi, is the earliest printed Scripture in a Kenyan language. Johann Ludwig Krapf of the Church Missionary Society prepared the translation at Rabai Mpia, the CMS station inland from Mombasa founded by Krapf and Johannes Rebmann in 1846.

Krapf had reached Mombasa in 1844 after years with the Lutheran and CMS missions at Ankober and Tajoura. His Swahili Matthew of 1844 had been the first East African Scripture. The Kamba portion was drawn from field speech collected during his 1849 journey inland as far as Kitui in Ukambani, guided by the caravan leader Kivoi wa Mwendwa. Krapf worked with Kamba informants at Rabai through 1849 and 1850 and sent the manuscript to London for CMS printing.

The edition is short: Mark alone, set in a plain Latin type without diacritics, distributed at Rabai and on the caravan routes that linked the coast with Ukambani. Kivoi was killed by Maasai raiders in 1851 during Krapf's second inland journey, and CMS work in Ukambani paused until the reopening of the mission in the 1890s. The Kamba New Testament was not completed until 1920 and the full Bible not until 1956.

he 1898 Luke in Kamba, titled Anyili wa Luka kwa kitungithyo cha Kikamba, is one of the earliest scriptural portions published in the Bantu language of the Ukambani highlands in present-day Kenya. The British and Foreign Bible Society issued it for the mission fields east of the Rift Valley, where the Africa Inland Mission had begun work among the Akamba in 1895. The volume transmits Luke alone, in a romanized orthography fitted to Kamba phonology, with the vernacular title following the BFBS convention for mission portions.

Kamba publication sat inside a wider BFBS program of Swahili-family and Bantu scriptures coordinated from the Society's London office and distributed through the Punjab, Egyptian, and East African auxiliaries. The Luke portion preceded a fuller New Testament translation effort that would take decades to complete. Copies circulated through mission stations at Kibwezi and Machakos, the early staging posts for inland evangelism from the Mombasa coast.

cts of the Apostles in Kikamba, the Bantu language of the Akamba people of eastern Kenya, printed by the British and Foreign Bible Society in 1904. The edition belongs to the early Kikamba Scripture sequence that opened with the Gospel of Mark in 1892 and continued through single-book portions before the first complete Kikamba New Testament of 1920.

The pioneering translation work was carried by the Africa Inland Mission, founded in 1895 by Peter Cameron Scott, and by the Church Missionary Society, both of which established stations in Ukambani in the last decade of the nineteenth century. The Acts volume carries the narrative of the early church in the Kikamba of its period, with Greek proper names adapted to Kamba phonology. his 1974 Kikamba Genesis was issued by the Bible Society of Kenya for Kamba-speaking readers across Machakos, Kitui, and Makueni districts in the dry hill country east of Nairobi. Kamba (ISO 639-3 kam) is an Eastern Bantu language of the Kenya highlands, closely related to Kikuyu, Meru, and Embu. Speaker estimates in the late twentieth century ran above three and a half million, making it one of the larger first languages of Kenya.

Christian scripture in Kikamba began with the African Inland Mission and the Church Missionary Society in the 1890s, and the first Gospels appeared in print at the Kibwezi and Mukaa stations in the early 1900s. A complete Kikamba New Testament was published in 1920, and the full Bible (Mbivilia Ndaa) followed in 1956 under the British and Foreign Bible Society. The Bible Society of Kenya, established as a national member of the United Bible Societies in 1971, took over reprinting and revision work shortly afterwards.

The 1974 Genesis sits in the early years of the Bible Society of Kenya's independent publishing programme, issued as a stand-alone book of the Pentateuch alongside its full-Bible reprints. Such single-book portions served Sunday school use and Bible study circles in the African Inland Church and other Kamba-speaking denominations in Eastern Province.

Presented as 61 chapters plus the complete film (2:01:44 in total). Kikamba is spoken mainly in Kenya by around 4,660,000 people.

items.title: The Beginning
items.description:
The story of Jesus fits within the larger story of the Judeo Christian tradition. The purpose of everything since creation has been to point to the life of Jesus.

All of creation speaks of the majesty of God. As God created man and woman he intended them to live in peace with him forever. But because of their disobedience mankind was separated from God. But God still loved mankind so throughout the Scriptures God reveals his plan to save the world.
items.description_short: The story of Jesus fits within the larger story of the Judeo Christian tradition. The purpose of everything since creation has been to point to the life of Jesus.

items.title: Birth Of Jesus
items.description:
Luke makes his introduction as the careful author of this Gospel. The angel Gabriel appears to Mary, a virgin in Nazareth. He announces to her that she has found favor with God and will give birth to Jesus, the Son of God.

Through Jesus' birth, prophecies are fulfilled by the arrangement of events. God leaves no detail unnoticed. The same can be said of our own lives.
items.description_short: Luke makes his introduction as the careful author of this Gospel. The angel Gabriel appears to Mary, a virgin in Nazareth. He announces to her that she has found favor with God and will give birth to Jesus, the Son of God.

items.title: Childhood Of Jesus
items.description:
One week after the baby is born, He is circumcised and officially named Jesus. While Jesus is a small boy they go to the temple where they meet a man named Simeon.

The Holy Spirit had assured Simeon he would not die before seeing the Lord's Messiah. Simeon sees Jesus and declares Him the promised Messiah.
items.description_short: One week after the baby is born, He is circumcised and officially named Jesus. While Jesus is a small boy they go to the temple where they meet a man named Simeon.

items.title: Baptism Of Jesus By John
items.description:
John the Baptist calls out in the desert. He preaches by the river Jordan, "Turn away from your sins and be baptized, and God will forgive your sins." He is the one Isaiah predicted would make way for the Lord. The crowds gather. Immediately, he warns them not to only say they have repented. Instead, they're to follow repentance with actions that exhibit a changed heart.

Jesus is baptized and receives the Holy Spirit. He kneels at the feet of someone lesser than Himself to be baptized. He demonstrates how we are to be humble.
items.description_short: John the Baptist calls out in the desert.

items.title: The Devil Tempts Jesus
items.description:
After Jesus has been baptized, He's led by the Spirit into the desert. He spends 40 days there, constantly tempted by the devil. All that time, he eats nothing. 

The devil tries to tempt Jesus, but Jesus answers using Scripture, resisting him.
items.description_short: After Jesus has been baptized, He's led by the Spirit into the desert. He spends 40 days there, constantly tempted by the devil. All that time, he eats nothing.

items.title: Jesus Proclaims Fulfillment Of The Scriptures
items.description:
When Jesus returns to Nazareth, He goes to the synagogue. He's asked to read the Scriptures and is handed the Book of Isaiah. From it, He reads Isaiah 61:1-2.

The prophecy speaks of bringing good news to the poor, proclaiming liberty to the captives, recovery of sight to the blind, freeing the oppressed, and announcing that it's time the Lord will save His people.

When He finishes reading, Jesus announces to the people that the prophecy has come true as it was just read.
items.description_short: When Jesus returns to Nazareth, He goes to the synagogue. He's asked to read the Scriptures and is handed the Book of Isaiah. From it, He reads Isaiah 61:1-2.

items.title: Parable Of The Pharisee And Tax Collector
items.description:
Jesus teaches from a boat off the shore of Lake Gennesaret. He speaks in parables, giving the example of a Pharisee and tax collector going to the temple to pray. The two men approach prayer very differently.

The Pharisee in the story stands by himself and lists his respectable attributes. He thanks God that he is not greedy, dishonest, or an adulterer like everyone else. He specifically points out the tax collector and thanks God for not being like him. The Pharisee boldly tells God what he does: He fasts two days a week and gives a tenth of his income.

The tax collector stands at a distance from the altar. Head bowed, he beats on his chest. The only thing he prays is, "God, have pity on me, a sinner!"
items.description_short: Jesus teaches from a boat off the shore of Lake Gennesaret. He speaks in parables, giving the example of a Pharisee and tax collector going to the temple to pray. The two men approach prayer very differently.

items.title: Miraculous Catch Of Fish
items.description:
Jesus tells the fisherman who owns it to push out farther and let down their nets. The fisherman grumbles that he and the others have already been out all night long. They didn't catch anything.

The fisherman agrees to go out and calls to his partners. Jesus sits in the boat with the fisherman. He waits expectantly. Then gathers the nets, slowly bringing something to the surface.

He laughs with joy when he sees the nets are full of flopping fish. 

When they're done, the fisherman sits in a boat full of fish. He looks up to Jesus. The fisherman frowns and says, "Go away from me, Lord. I am a sinful man." Jesus tells him not to be afraid, that from then on, he would be a fisher of men.
items.description_short: Jesus tells the fisherman who owns it to push out farther and let down their nets. The fisherman grumbles that he and the others have already been out all night long. They didn't catch anything.

items.title: Jairuss Daughter Brought Back To Life
items.description:
Crowds press in on Jesus as He leaves the synagogue. One voice rises above the others. A man, Jairus, begs Jesus to save his sick, 12-year-old daughter. 

Another man runs up to Jairus. He tells him not to bother the teacher, that his daughter has died. Jesus turns and tells him not to be afraid. And that if Jairus would believe, his daughter would be well.

Jesus and the disciples visit the family. The neighbors wail for the loss of the daughter. She lies lifeless on a cot. Jesus looks at her for a moment. Then He looks to the child’s mother and comforts her. He says the child isn't dead, but that she’s actually just asleep. 

Jesus sits and looks at the girl for a moment, then tells her to rise.
items.description_short: Crowds press in on Jesus as He leaves the synagogue. One voice rises above the others. A man, Jairus, begs Jesus to save his sick, 12-year-old daughter.

items.title: Disciples Chosen
items.description:
Jesus spots a tax collector named Matthew Levi at the gate. He collects toll money for customs as people pass through. As Jesus looks at him, Matthew senses it and looks up. Jesus says, "Follow me."

Matthew watches Him go for a moment. Silently, he stands and leaves everything to follow Jesus. Later Jesus goes up a hill to pray. He prays the entire night to God. When He comes down from the hill the next morning, He gathers His followers. From them, he chooses 12 apostles.

Simon (who Jesus named Peter) and Simon's brother Andrew had been the fishermen who experienced the miracle of a large catch of fish. Then Jesus chooses James and John, Philip and Bartholomew. And He chooses Matthew, the tax collector he had called at the gate. And finally Jesus chooses Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who would betray Jesus.
items.description_short: Jesus spots a tax collector named Matthew Levi at the gate. He collects toll money for customs as people pass through. As Jesus looks at him, Matthew senses it and looks up. Jesus says, "Follow me."

items.title: Beatitudes
items.description:
Jesus looks out over the crowds gathered to hear him speak. But instead of speaking to the masses, Jesus turns back to his disciples. He encourages them for the journey ahead.

He assures them that they are blessed when people hate them, reject them, insult them, and say that they are evil because they follow Jesus. He encourages them to be happy and dance for joy when that happens. Because there will be great reward in heaven for them. And He reminds them that their ancestors acted the same way toward prophets.
items.description_short: Jesus looks out over the crowds who have gathered to hear him speak. But instead of speaking to the masses, Jesus turns back to his disciples. He encourages them for the journey ahead.

items.title: Sermon On The Mount
items.description: Jesus turns to the crowds and walks through them, teaching. He advises everyone how to walk through life in love. And talks of how, out of pride, we often judge others. He implores those who are listening to love their enemies, to actively pray for them. He speaks of offering more than what is asked of you. Do for others what you would have them do for you.

items.title: Blessed Are Those Who Hear And Obey
items.description: Jesus reminds us that those who hear and obey are blessed.

items.title: Sinful Woman Forgiven
items.description:
A Pharisee invites Jesus to have dinner at His house. They're eating when a woman approaches Jesus. Everyone in the house stares, including the Pharisee. 

Jesus tells the Pharisee a story. He says that there were two men who owed money to someone. One owed 500 silver coins. The other owed 50. Neither men could pay their debt. So the lender canceled both debts. Jesus asks which man loved the lender more for what he'd done.
items.description_short: A Pharisee invites Jesus to have dinner at His house. They're eating when a woman approaches Jesus. Everyone in the house stares, including the Pharisee.

items.title: Women Disciples
items.description: Jesus continues through the countryside. He's adamant in preaching the good news about the kingdom of God. The twelve disciples follow him. And some women follow as well. They serve the disciples, using their own resources to aid the ministry of Jesus.
items.description_short: Jesus continues through the countryside. He's adamant in preaching the good news about the kingdom of God. The twelve disciples follow him. And some women follow as well.

items.title: John The Baptist In Prison
items.description:
Herod has thrown John the Baptist into prison. Messengers come to him in the prison. They relay to him all that Jesus has been doing.

Specifically, they tell him about a funeral procession where Jesus sees the widow who has lost her son. His heart fills with compassion. He tells the young man to get up! The son rises from the dead and goes back with his mother.

After hearing this, John asks them to go ask Jesus if He's the Messiah, or if they should expect someone else. The messengers arrive where Jesus is sleeping and ask Him what John wants to know.
items.description_short: Herod has thrown John the Baptist into prison. Messengers come to him in the prison. They relay to him all that Jesus has been doing.

items.title: Parable Of The Sower And The Seed
items.description:
The crowds press in on Jesus as He walks and teaches. He tells a parable of someone sowing seeds of grain in a field. The seed falls in a number of places, each representing something to the crowd.

A disciple asks Jesus why He speaks in parables. Jesus explains the parable to the disciples. The seed that's scattered is the Word of God.
items.description_short: The crowds press in on Jesus as He walks and teaches. He tells a parable of someone sowing seeds of grain in a field. The seed falls in a number of places, each representing something to the crowd.

items.title: Parable Of The Lamp
items.description:
Jesus uses a torch to explain how his followers should live. No one covers the light or puts it under a bed. Instead, they put it in a place where people will see the light when they come in. 

He goes on to say that whatever is kept a secret will be brought into the open. And anything that's covered up will be found and brought into the light.
items.description_short: Jesus uses a torch to explain how his followers should live. No one covers the light or puts it under a bed. Instead, they put it in a place where people will see the light when they come in.

items.title: Jesus Calms The Storm
items.description:
Jesus gets into a boat and tells His disciples they should all go to the other side of the lake. Along the way, Jesus falls asleep. A storm starts to rage. Waves stretch high over the bow. And the boat starts to take on water.

The whole time, Jesus stays asleep. The disciples hold on tight. They try to keep the boat afloat. Finally, Peter cries out to the still sleeping Jesus. He tells Jesus that the boat is taking on water and that they'll all be drowned.

Jesus stands and puts a hand out toward the storm. The storm clears. And the seas immediately calm.
items.description_short: Jesus gets into a boat and tells His disciples they should all go to the other side of the lake. Along the way, Jesus falls asleep. A storm starts to rage. Waves stretch high over the bow. And the boat starts to take on water.

items.title: Healing Of The Demoniac
items.description:
Jesus and His disciples continue to sail and arrive at Gerasa. A wild man on the shore growls at their approach. Jesus hurries toward him, ahead of His disciples.

The man threatens Jesus with the rock. But Jesus just continues to stare at him. The man calls Jesus by name and declares Him to be the Son of God. Jesus asks him his name. At first the man won't say. But Jesus holds out a hand to him. He says his name is Legion. He begs not to be sent back to the abyss. Instead, he wants to go into a nearby herd of pigs. Jesus puts a hand out to the pigs.
items.description_short: Jesus and His disciples continue to sail and arrive at Gerasa. A wild man on the shore growls at their approach. Jesus hurries toward him, ahead of His disciples.

items.title: Jesus Feeds 5000
items.description:
Jesus and the disciples continue to walk the countryside. And a great crowd follows them. Peter comes and asks Jesus to send the people away.

He wants them to find food and a place to stay with local farmers and villagers. Jesus looks back out over the crowd of people. They want to hear from Jesus and have sacrificed to be there. Jesus considers this and tells the disciples to feed the people.

Mary Magdalene points out that they only have a few loaves of bread and two fish. Jesus takes the baskets and proclaims to the heavens and the people, "Blessed is the Lord God, King of the Universe who brings forth bread from the earth."
items.description_short: Jesus and the disciples continue to walk the countryside. And a great crowd follows them. Peter comes and asks Jesus to send the people away.

items.title: Peter Declares Jesus To Be The Christ
items.description:
Jesus asks who the crowds say He is. Peter speaks up immediately. He claims that some in the crowds say Jesus is John the Baptist. Others say He's Elijah.

Others say that one of the prophets from centuries ago has come back to life. Jesus solemnly asks who Peter would say He is. Without hesitation, Peter says Jesus is God's Messiah. Jesus stares back at him.
items.description_short: Jesus asks who the crowds say He is. Peter speaks up immediately. He claims that some in the crowds say Jesus is John the Baptist. Others say He's Elijah.

items.title: The Transfiguration
items.description:
Jesus takes John, James and Peter up a hill to pray. Jesus walks apart from them, covering His head to pray. But when He does, His appearance changes.

His face changes. His clothes become pure white. He starts talking to two men who seem to be with Him. Moses and Elijah speak to Him. One says Jesus will fulfill God's purpose. The other says He will die in Jerusalem. Peter slowly wakes up. He's the first to see Moses and Elijah talking with Jesus. He wakes James and John. They see it too.

Moses and Elijah turn and leave, fading away. The disciples fall to their knees and worship Jesus.
items.description_short: Jesus takes John, James and Peter up a hill to pray. Jesus walks apart from them, covering His head to pray. But when He does, His appearance changes.

items.title: Jesus Heals Boy From Evil Spirit
items.description:
The crowds continue to gather. They wait on Jesus. Finally, Jesus comes down the hill with Peter, James and John. One man approaches Jesus and begs that Jesus would heal his son.

The boy writhes on the ground. The man goes on to say that the boy is his only son. He asked the disciples to cast out the demon. But they couldn't. Jesus gently tells the man to bring his son closer.

Two men carry the boy to Jesus. But he falls again into another fit. Jesus comes to stand over him. The boy looks up. And slowly, he gets up. Now, where there were cuts and bruises on his face, there are none.
items.description_short: The crowds continue to gather. They wait on Jesus. Finally, Jesus comes down the hill with Peter, James and John. One man approaches Jesus and begs that Jesus would heal his son.

items.title: The Lords Prayer
items.description: The followers of Jesus clean up and take a break at a stream. Jesus stands nearby, praying. Andrew asks Jesus to teach them to pray.

items.title: Teaching About Prayer And Faith
items.description:
Jesus has just taught them how to pray. He says, "ask and you will receive." He implores them to seek and assures that they will find.

He reminds His followers that none of them would give their children bad things when they ask for good things. He says that no matter how bad mankind is, we still know to give good gifts to our children. And that the Heavenly Father will all the more give the Holy Spirit to those who ask.
items.description_short: Jesus has just taught them how to pray. He says, "ask and you will receive." He challenges them to seek and assures that they will find.

items.title: Woe To Those Who Cause Others To Sin
items.description:
As Jesus and the disciples continue to walk the countryside he tells them that there will be temptation. There will be situations which cause people to sin. But the disciples should never be the cause.

He looks into the crowd and says it would be better for that person to have a large stone hung around his neck and be tossed into the sea. That would be better than causing someone else to stumble in or lose their faith.
items.description_short: As Jesus and the disciples continue to walk the countryside he tells them that there will be temptation. There will be situations which cause people to sin. But the disciples should never be the cause.

items.title: The Kingdom Of God As A Mustard Seed
items.description: Jesus tells the people that the kingdom of God is like a grain of mustard seed. Farmers plant seeds in their field. From it, a tree grows. And when the tree is big enough, birds sit in its branches.

items.title: Jesus Spends Time With Sinners
items.description:
As Jesus sits with a group of people in a village a man walks up and angrily asks why Jesus sits with those who aren't respectable people. Jesus responds that people who are well don't need a doctor.

He hasn't come to ask "respectable" people to ask forgiveness for what they do. But He would ask the outcasts to seek and find forgiveness.
items.description_short: As Jesus sits with a group of people in a village a man walks up and angrily asks why Jesus sits with those who aren't respectable people. Jesus responds that people who are well don't need a doctor.

items.title: Healing On The Sabbath
items.description:
A boy asks Jesus to tell them more about the kingdom. Jesus teaches in the synagogue that believers shouldn't fear. That God is pleased to give them the kingdom. They can feel free to give because their treasure is somewhere else.

He urges them to sell their possessions and give to people. He insists that they can make a treasure in heaven that will never wear out. He says that the treasure follows the heart and where it is.
items.description_short: A boy asks Jesus to tell them more about the kingdom. Jesus teaches in the synagogue that believers shouldn't fear. That God is pleased to give them the kingdom. They can feel free to give because their treasure is somewhere else.

items.title: Parable Of The Good Samaritan
items.description:
A man asks Jesus what they should do. Jesus asks what the Scriptures say. The man replies with, "Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind, and love your neighbor as yourself." 

Jesus tells him that if they do this, they will have life. But then someone asks, "Who is my neighbor?"
items.description_short: A man asks Jesus what they should do. Jesus asks what the Scriptures say. The man replies with, "Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind, and love your neighbor as yourself."

items.title: Healing Of Bartimaeus
items.description:
Jesus and His disciples wade through a stream into a gathering of people. A man asks what's going on. He follows after Jesus, calling out to Him.

John comes back for the man and helps him back to Jesus. The blind man calls Jesus the Son of David and begs for mercy. Jesus asks what the man wants Him to do. And the man answers that he would like to see again.
items.description_short: Jesus and His disciples wade through a stream into a gathering of people. A man asks what's going on. He follows after Jesus, calling out to Him.

items.title: Jesus And Zaccheus
items.description:
Jesus enters the town surrounded by crowds pushing in on Him. Zacchaeus, a short man, tries to see Jesus. But he can't see above the crowds or get through them. He climbs a tree. Jesus calls out to him.

He tells Zacchaeus to come down from the tree because He wants to have dinner with him. People are appalled. Zacchaeus is the town tax collector. But Zacchaeus is more than happy. He comes down from the tree and leads the way.
items.description_short: Jesus enters the town surrounded by crowds pushing in on Him. Zacchaeus, a short man, tries to see Jesus. But he can't see above the crowds or get through them. He climbs a tree. Jesus calls out to him.

items.title: Jesus Predicts His Death And Resurrection
items.description: Jesus continues to sit at dinner with His disciples. He asks them to listen carefully. He tells them plainly that they're all going to Jerusalem with Him. And that everything the prophets wrote about the Son of Man will come true.

items.title: Jesuss Triumphal Entry
items.description:
Jesus starts on the road to Jerusalem. Just outside Jerusalem, there are crowds with palm branches and a donkey. He climbs onto the donkey and makes His way toward Jerusalem. The crowds yell and cheer.

The people lay blankets and palm leaves down as a path for Jesus. Some Pharisees in the crowd block the path. They tell Jesus to quiet His disciples. But Jesus laughs. He tells them that if the crowds were quiet, the stones themselves would cry out.
items.description_short: Jesus starts on the road to Jerusalem. Just outside Jerusalem, there are crowds with palm branches and a donkey. He climbs onto the donkey and makes His way toward Jerusalem. The crowds yell and cheer.

items.title: Jesus Weeps Over Jerusalem
items.description: Jesus, His disciples, and a large crowd of followers approach Jerusalem. When it's in sight, Jesus stops and looks out over it. He talks of how Jerusalem could not see and understand a path to peace.

items.title: Jesus Drives Out Money Changers
items.description:
Jesus walks through Jerusalem. Crowds of people move with Him. He enters the temple and looks around. There are men counting money to each other. And people carry around goods to be sold.

He continues to look at the people and the business exchange that's happening in the temple. He walks up and overthrows one money-changer's table. Then another. And another.

Jesus charges back into the courtyard area and yells at them. He says that the temple is to be a house of prayer. But they've turned it into a den of thieves.
items.description_short: Jesus walks through Jerusalem. Crowds of people move with Him. He enters the temple and looks around. There are men counting money to each other. And people carry around goods to be sold.

items.title: Widows Offering
items.description:
In the temple, Jesus watches a widow give all that she has. People in the crowd note how little she gives. They ask for her to give more. 

But Jesus proclaims to everyone that the widow gave more than everyone else. Everyone else who contributed gave out of the extra money they had. But the widow, even in her poverty, gave everything she owned.
items.description_short: In the temple, Jesus watches a widow give all that she has. People in the crowd note how little she gives. They ask for her to give more.

items.title: Annas Questions Jesuss Authority
items.description:
A Pharisee named Annas asks Jesus what right He has to say the kinds of things he says. In return, Jesus asks Annas a question.

Jesus asks whether John's right to baptize came from God or from man. Annas turns with other Pharisees and talks to them.

So they go back to Jesus and answer that they don't know who gave John the right to baptize. Jesus stares back. He says since they don't know, he won't tell them who gave Him the authority to teach the things He's been teaching.
items.description_short: A Pharisee named Annas asks Jesus what right He has to say the kinds of things he says. In return, Jesus asks Annas a question.

items.title: Parable Of The Vineyard And Tenants
items.description:
Jesus tells the story of a man who plants a vineyard. That man leases the vineyard to workers or tenants.

Jesus shares the verse that the stone the builders rejected would become the most important one. He goes on to state that anyone who falls on that stone will be broken. And if that stone falls on anyone, it will crush that person.
items.description_short: Jesus tells the story of a man who plants a vineyard. That man leases the vineyard to workers or tenants.

items.title: Paying Taxes To Caesar
items.description:
The Pharisees tell Jesus they know He teaches right things. They say Jesus doesn't pay attention to anyone's status. But that Jesus teaches the truth about God's will for all people. And then they ask about paying taxes.

The Pharisee asks Jesus whether or not it's right that they pay taxes to Caesar. Jesus asks the Pharisees to show him a silver coin.
items.description_short: The Pharisees tell Jesus they know He teaches righteous things. But, they also say Jesus doesn't pay attention to anyone elses status. But that Jesus teaches the truth about God's will for all people. And then they ask about paying taxes.

items.title: The Last Supper
items.description:
Passover is about to begin. Jesus sends Peter and John ahead to prepare the Passover meal. Jesus sits with them and looks at all of them. He tells them how glad He is to share the meal before he suffers.

Jesus takes his cup and prays to God. As when He prayed over the bread and fish, He thanks God for the blessing of the fruit of the vine that God brings forth. He passes it to the nearest disciple and tells them all to drink it.

Jesus reaches for a piece of bread and prays again. He thanks God for bringing bread from the earth and breaks it. He passes the two pieces to the disciples and claims that the bread represents His body that's given for them. They should eat and remember Him. The cup is still being passed around. Jesus says that the cup of wine is a new testament in His blood and it's shed for them.
items.description_short: Passover is about to begin. Jesus sends Peter and John ahead to prepare the Passover meal. Jesus sits with them and looks at all of them. He tells them how glad He is to share the meal before he suffers.

items.title: Upper Room Teaching
items.description:
Jesus sits after sharing the bread and wine, sealing a new covenant with His followers, and revealing that there is a traitor among them. He passes on one last specific teaching to His disciples. The disciples listen solemnly.

He tells them that the greatest of them must be like the least of them. And the leader must be like the servant. He asks which one is actually greater: the one who sits down at the table or the one who serves? He says that the one who sits is greater. But then He points out that He Himself came as one who serves.
items.description_short: Jesus sits after sharing the bread and wine, sealing a new covenant with His followers, and revealing that there is a traitor among them. He passes on one last specific teaching to His disciples. The disciples listen solemnly.

items.title: Jesus Is Betrayed And Arrested
items.description:
The council of the Jewish elders meets to see how they can get rid of Jesus. Meanwhile, Jesus sits with the rest of His followers and tells them to pray against temptation.

Judas arrives at the council and counts out his pieces of silver. Jesus walks off alone so that He can pray. He asks His Heavenly Father to take the burden of His cup away from Him. But He says He'd rather have God's will than His own be done. As Jesus continues to pray, His sweat became like great drops of blood. He rises from prayer and returns to the disciples. But they're asleep.

 A crowd of Jews approaches Him. Judas leads the way and gets close to Jesus. He kisses Him on the cheek. The disciples lunge forward asking if they should go to battle. Peter runs forward and cuts the ear off one of the men. Jesus heals the man and stops the brawl. He asks why they come with clubs. And Jesus is arrested.
items.description_short: The council of the Jewish elders meet to see how they can get rid of Jesus. Meanwhile, Jesus sits with the rest of His followers and tells them to pray against temptation.

items.title: Peter Disowns Jesus
items.description:
Jesus is taken to the house of the high priest and guarded by temple guards. They push Him and take His clothing in the courtyard. Peter watches from close by.

Peter is recognized, but denies that He knows Jesus. As dawn approaches, a rooster crows. Jesus looks over to Peter. Peter walks away, undone by his denials.
items.description_short: Jesus is taken to the house of the high priest and guarded by temple guards. They push Him and take His clothing in the courtyard. Peter watches from close by.

items.title: Jesus Is Mocked And Questioned
items.description:
Jesus gets beaten by the temple guards. A man tells the guards to bring Jesus in to see the council.

Annas and Caiaphas enter. The room is full of other Jewish men. They want to know if Jesus is the Messiah. Jesus only replies that if He tells them, the council won't believe Him. He says the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of God.

They ask if He is the Son of God. Jesus replies that they say He is. They don't know what to make of His answer. One of them stands and acts as a witness. Everyone heard His replies. The council decides to take Him to Pilate.
items.description_short: Jesus gets beaten by the temple guards. A man tells the guards to bring Jesus in to see the council.

items.title: Jesus Is Brought To Pilate
items.description:
Roman guards open the gates and take Jesus. They march through the courtyard followed by the crowd. Pontius Pilate marches out. He's known as the most vicious Roman governor, responsible for the crucifixion of thousands.

Pilate demands to know what they want. The Jewish crowd yells that Jesus is confusing their people and that Jesus upset the temple market. They demand a sentence from Pilate.

Pilate asks Jesus if he is the King of the Jews. Jesus only replies, "So you say.&quot
items.description_short: Roman guards open the gates and take Jesus. They march through the courtyard followed by the crowd. Pontius Pilate, the most vicious Roman governor who is responsible for the crucifixion of thousands, come to address the crowd.

items.title: Jesus Is Brought To Herod
items.description:
Jesus is escorted into Herod's presence. Herod looks Him up and down then asks, "Who is it that you say you are?" Jesus remains silent. 

Herod says that he's heard that Jesus can perform miracles and signs. Herod demands that Jesus do something for him. But Jesus stays silent and unmoving.
items.description_short: Jesus is escorted into Herod's presence. Herod looks Him up and down then asks, "Who is it that you say you are?" Jesus remains silent.

items.title: Jesus Is Sentenced
items.description:
Jesus is dragged from Herod's palace. Jesus and the crowds come back to Pilate's courtyard. 

He sits in the judgment seat and says he will only order that Jesus be scourged. The council speaks up again. They remind Pilate that he is supposed to release one man to the Jews during the Passover Festival.

The guards tie Jesus to a pole in the center of the courtyard and start to whip Him with cat o' nine tails that rip the flesh from His back. Pilate watches the courtyard warily before he leaves.

Pilate makes his way back with a scroll. Jesus is released and dragged back in front of Pilate. He drops the crucifixion judgment at Jesus's feet.
items.description_short: Jesus is dragged from Herod's palace. Jesus and the crowds come back to Pilate's courtyard.

items.title: Jesus Carries His Cross
items.description:
Jesus carries His own cross beam through the streets. The Roman guards beat back those in their path. Jesus continues to struggle under the weight of the beam.

He collapses in the street, falling to His knees. A Roman guard looks over the crowd and sees a big man. He is forced to carry the beam while Jesus stumbles along. The crowds yell angrily. But some mourn.

Jesus urges them to weep for themselves because there are harder times coming. The Romans push Jesus along after them, prodding Him forward when He stops or stumbles.
items.description_short: Jesus struggles to carry His own cross beam through the streets, while the Roman guards beat those out of the way in their path. Jesus continues to struggle under the weight of the beam.

items.title: Jesus Is Crucified
items.description:
They arrive at the place where the crosses are being set up. Others are being tied to their crosses. Jesus is stripped and led to His own cross. They throw Him down on it. There are cries as the others are nailed to their crosses.

The nails are hammered through Jesus's wrists and feet as He screams. Then slowly, the crosses are erected as Romans pulls the ropes. Jesus is lifted high in the air. He hangs on the cross, tired and in pain. He prays for those in the crowd. He asks God to forgive them because they don't know what they do.

The crowd murmurs at the feet of the cross. Annas and Caiaphas comment that He saved others. They wonder why He doesn't save Himself. The crowd starts to jeer. They urge Him to save Himself. But He doesn't.
items.description_short: They arrive at the place where the crosses are being set up. Others are being tied to their crosses. Jesus is stripped and led to His own cross. They throw Him down on it. There are cries as the others are nailed to their crosses.

items.title: Soldiers Gamble For Jesuss Clothes
items.description:
As Jesus continues to hang on the cross, the crowd watches in silence. The Roman guards gather around the cross and watch Jesus.

A Roman claims that the clothing is no regular garment. He tosses it to the group of guards. They yell and debate who will get it. One suggests they play, or gamble, for it.
items.description_short: As Jesus continues to hang on the cross, the crowd watches in silence. The Roman guards gather around the cross and watch Jesus.

items.title: Sign On The Cross
items.description:
The Roman guard takes a sign and hammers it above Jesus's head. The crowd erupts with laughing and yelling. The guard tries to give Him vinegar from a sponge.

The guard insists He save Himself if He's really King of the Jews. The crowd continues to yell. But there are a few who look on and cry.
items.description_short: The Roman guard hammers a sign of mockery above Jesus's head. The crowd erupts with laughing and yelling. Then, the guard tries to give Him vinegar from a sponge.

items.title: Crucified Convicts
items.description:
Jesus hangs between two other men. His disciples watch, helpless. One of the men on a cross asks if Jesus is the Messiah. He tells Him to save Himself and them.

The other man on a cross tells him that Jesus receives the same sentence as those who are guilty. But He did nothing wrong. The man asks Jesus to remember him when he comes back as King. Jesus promises the man that he will be in paradise with Jesus.
items.description_short: Jesus hangs between two other men. His disciples watch, helpless. One of the men on a cross asks if Jesus is the Messiah. He tells Him to save Himself and them.

items.title: Death Of Jesus
items.description:
Jesus continues to hang on the cross. Darkness comes over everything. The veil in the temple is torn right down the middle. 

Jesus breathes heavily. He prays and gives up His spirit willingly into the Father’s hand. And then He dies.
items.description_short: Jesus continues to hang on the cross. Darkness comes over everything. The veil in the temple is torn right down the middle.

items.title: Burial Of Jesus
items.description: Joseph of Arimathea asks Pontius Pilate for permission to bury Jesus in a tomb. He receives permission. He and a servant carry the body into the tomb and lay it down on a rocky shelf. Joseph covers the exposed, bloody foot of Jesus and sprinkles dirt on Him.
items.description_short: Joseph of Arimathea asks Pontius Pilate for permission to bury Jesus in a tomb.

items.title: Angels At The Tomb
items.description:
The sun rises the Sunday after the Sabbath. The women return with spices they had prepared. But when they get close, they see the rock has been moved.

Jesus's body is gone. The linens He was wrapped in still lay there, though. Two angels appear and the women bow. They ask why the women look for someone living in the place of the dead. The angels state that Jesus has risen.
items.description_short: The sun rises the Sunday after the Sabbath. The women return with spices they had prepared. But when they get close, they see the rock has been moved.

items.title: The Tomb Is Empty
items.description:
Mary Magdalene rushes into a room full of disciples. She tells the men the stone has been rolled away. And that when she and the others went into the tomb, the body was gone.

Joanna speaks of the angels. She says there were two shining men. And they told the women not to look for the living among the dead.

Peter rushes away and to the tomb. He runs in and walks right to the rocky shelf. But there's no body. There's only the linen. He kneels and takes it in his hands. He shuffles it, looking through it. But after a moment he stops. He sighs and bows his head.
items.description_short: Mary Magdalene rushes into a room full of disciples. She tells the men the stone has been rolled away. And that when she and the others went into the tomb, the body was gone.

items.title: Resurrected Jesus Appears
items.description:
John and others return to the room where Jesus's followers have gathered. They come in saying that Jesus has indeed risen. John says Jesus appeared to Simon on the road. Simon talks about how they didn't recognize Jesus at first.

But when they sat down to dinner and Jesus broke the bread, they knew who He was.

Jesus stands in the room with them. He asks why they're troubled and doubtful. He holds out His hands for them to see. He encourages them to touch Him to prove to them that He's flesh and blood. They reach out and touch His hands.
items.description_short: John and others return to the room where Jesus' followers have gathered. They come in saying that Jesus has indeed risen! John says that Jesus appeared to Simon on the road. Simon talks about how they did not recognize Jesus at first.

items.title: Great Commission And Ascension
items.description:
The men and women follow Jesus down a hill. He says all power has been given to Him in heaven and on earth. So the followers are to go and teach the nations.

He tells them to baptize in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. He says to teach people how to do everything He taught them. And that He will be with them always.
items.description_short: The men and women follow Jesus down a hill. He says all power has been given to Him in heaven and on earth. So the followers are to go and teach the nations.

items.title: Invitation To Know Jesus Personally
items.description:
A narrator gives an invitation to know God personally.

The invitation is open to everyone. It means turning to God and trusting Jesus with our lives and to forgive our sins. We can speak to Him in prayer when we're ready to become followers of Jesus.
items.description_short: A narrator gives an invitation to know God personally.

original.title: JESUS
original.film_description:
This film is a perfect introduction to Jesus through the Gospel of Luke. Jesus constantly surprises and confounds people, from His miraculous birth to His rise from the grave. Follow His life through excerpts from the Book of Luke, all the miracles, the teachings, and the passion. 

God creates everything and loves mankind. But mankind disobeys God. God and mankind are separated, but God loves mankind so much, He arranges redemption for mankind. He sends his Son Jesus to be a perfect sacrifice to make amends for us.

Before Jesus arrives, God prepares mankind. Prophets speak of the birth, the life, and the death of Jesus.

Jesus attracts attention. He teaches in parables no one really understands, gives sight to the blind, and helps those who no one sees as worth helping.

He scares the Jewish leaders, they see him as a threat. So they arrange, through Judas the traitor and their Roman oppressors, for the crucifixion of Jesus. They think the matter is settled. But the women who serve Jesus discover an empty tomb. The disciples panic. When Jesus appears, they doubt He's real. But it's what He proclaimed all along: He is their perfect sacrifice, their Savior, victor over death. He ascends to heaven, telling His followers to tell others about Him and His teachings.
